hints: Hint 1: Look at each cell type in the lists and ask, does it have a nucleus and is it a eukaryotic cell? Mitosis needs both.
Hint 2: Remember how bacteria divide, and remember which human blood cell loses its nucleus when mature and so cannot divide at all.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall what mitosis needs**
Mitosis is division of a eukaryotic nucleus to make two genetically identical nuclei. So only eukaryotic cells with a nucleus can do it.

Think: no nucleus, no mitosis.

Step 2: **Rule out bacterial cells**
Bacteria are prokaryotes. They have no true nucleus and no mitotic spindle.

They divide by a simpler process called binary fission, not mitosis. So any group with bacterial cells is wrong. That removes A and B.

Step 3: **Rule out mature red blood cells**
Mature mammalian red blood cells have lost their nucleus to make more room for haemoglobin. Without DNA and without a nucleus, they cannot divide by mitosis.

That removes C, leaving D. Check D: cancer cells divide rapidly and uncontrollably by mitosis, lymphocytes divide by mitosis during clonal expansion, and stem cells divide by mitosis for growth and repair. All three fit.

options.A: Incorrect because bacterial cells are prokaryotes and divide by binary fission, not mitosis, even though cancer cells and stem cells do divide by mitosis.
options.B: Incorrect because bacterial cells cannot carry out mitosis, even though both lymphocytes and stem cells can.
options.C: Incorrect because mature red blood cells have no nucleus and so cannot divide at all, even though cancer cells and lymphocytes can divide by mitosis.
options.D: Correct because all three are nucleated eukaryotic cells that divide by mitosis: cancer cells uncontrollably, lymphocytes in an immune response, and stem cells for growth and repair.
